intro: Hi, welcome to FluentPath! In this first lesson we'll learn the names of English letters, find the vowels, and spell words out loud — useful every time you give your name or email. Warm-up: can you write your first name, letter by letter, with a dash between letters? (Example: B-U-D-I)
teachingNotes: Learners know the Latin alphabet from Indonesian, but the English letter NAMES differ: e.g. A is /eɪ/ (not 'a'), E is /iː/, I is /aɪ/, G is /dʒiː/, J is /dʒeɪ/.
Text-only lesson: describe letter names with sound-alike words (C sounds like 'see', I like 'eye', Y like 'why').
Spelling practice: learners write letters separated by dashes, e.g. C-A-T.
Common confusions for Indonesian speakers: E vs I, G vs J, A vs E.

Separate a letter's NAME from its SOUND. The name is what you say when spelling (A = 'ay'); inside a word the letter often sounds different (apple starts with an 'e'-like sound, cat with a 'k' sound, umbrella with an 'a' sound). Say this explicitly whenever an example word doesn't start with the letter's name.

Vowel = huruf vokal (huruf hidup), consonant = huruf konsonan (huruf mati). Y is counted as a consonant letter (yes, yellow), but in my and happy it makes a vowel sound; say that it 'borrows' a vowel sound so the two statements don't seem to contradict each other.
Z is 'zed' in British English and 'zee' in American English; both are correct.

keyPoints.title: Letter names are different from Indonesian
keyPoints.explanation: English letter names sound different. A sounds like 'ay' (as in 'day'), E like 'ee' (as in 'see'), I like 'eye', G like 'jee', J like 'jay'.

id.title: Nama huruf berbeda dari bahasa Indonesia
id.explanation: Nama huruf dalam bahasa Inggris bunyinya berbeda. A dibaca 'ei' (seperti di 'day'), E dibaca 'i' (seperti di 'see'), I dibaca 'ai' (seperti 'eye'), G dibaca 'ji', J dibaca 'jei'.

keyPoints.title: Five vowels
keyPoints.explanation: The vowel letters are A, E, I, O and U. Every other letter, Y too, is a consonant. Y is still a consonant letter, but in some words it borrows a vowel sound, as in 'my' ('ai').

examples.id: Huruf vokal: A, E, I, O, U

examples.en: b-O-O-k has two vowels: O and O

id.title: Lima huruf vokal
id.explanation: Huruf vokal adalah A, E, I, O, dan U. Semua huruf lain, termasuk Y, adalah konsonan. Y tetap huruf konsonan, tapi di beberapa kata Y 'meminjam' bunyi vokal, seperti di 'my' ('mai').

keyPoints.title: Spelling aloud
keyPoints.explanation: To spell a word, say each letter name in order. For double letters you can say 'double': B-O-O-K is 'B, double O, K'.

id.title: Mengeja dengan suara
id.explanation: Untuk mengeja kata, sebutkan nama tiap huruf secara berurutan. Untuk huruf ganda kamu bisa bilang 'double': B-O-O-K dibaca 'B, double O, K'.

material.title: Letter names are not Indonesian letter names

blocks.text: English uses the same 26 letters as Indonesian, but most of them have **different names**. When someone asks you to spell your name, they expect the English names.

id.text: Bahasa Inggris memakai 26 huruf yang sama dengan bahasa Indonesia, tetapi kebanyakan **namanya berbeda**. Saat seseorang memintamu mengeja nama, yang dipakai adalah nama huruf versi Inggris.

blocks.text: The pairs that confuse Indonesian speakers most are **E/I**, **G/J** and **A/R**. Say them slowly in pairs: E–I, G–J, A–R. And **Z** has two names: **zed** in British English and **zee** in American English. Both are correct.

id.text: Pasangan yang paling sering tertukar bagi penutur bahasa Indonesia adalah **E/I**, **G/J** dan **A/R**. Ucapkan pelan-pelan berpasangan: E–I, G–J, A–R. Lalu **Z** punya dua nama: **zed** dalam bahasa Inggris British dan **zee** ('zi') dalam bahasa Inggris Amerika. Keduanya benar.

blocks.prompt: Which letter's name sounds like the word 'why'?
blocks.explain: Y is said 'why'. W is 'double-you' and I is 'eye'.

id.explain: Y dibaca 'wai', seperti 'why'. W dibaca 'dabel-yu' dan I dibaca 'ai'.
id.prompt: Nama huruf mana yang bunyinya seperti kata 'why'?

id.title: Nama huruf berbeda dari bahasa Indonesia

material.title: A letter's name and its sound

blocks.text:
Every English letter has a **name** and a **sound**, and they are often different.
- The **name** is what you say when you **spell**: A is 'ei', C is 'si'.
- The **sound** is how the letter sounds **inside a word**: in *apple* the A sounds like 'e', in *cat* the C sounds like 'k'.

In Indonesian a letter's name and its sound are almost the same (a is 'a', k is 'ka'), so this feels strange at first. Remember: **spelling** a word → say the letter **names**. **Reading** a word → say the **sounds**.

id.text:
Setiap huruf bahasa Inggris punya **nama** dan **bunyi**, dan keduanya sering berbeda.
- **Nama** huruf dipakai saat kamu **mengeja**: A dibaca 'ei', C dibaca 'si'.
- **Bunyi** huruf adalah suaranya **di dalam kata**: di *apple* huruf A berbunyi 'e', di *cat* huruf C berbunyi 'k'.

Di bahasa Indonesia nama dan bunyi huruf hampir sama (a dibaca 'a', k dibaca 'ka'), jadi awalnya ini terasa aneh. Ingat: saat **mengeja** → sebut **nama** hurufnya. Saat **membaca** kata → ucapkan **bunyinya**.

id.note: di sini nama dan bunyinya mirip

blocks.text: Two more things that surprise learners. **W** is called 'double-you' (*dabel-yu*) because long ago it was written as two U's side by side. And one letter can have different sounds in different words; you'll practise the hardest ones in the next lesson. For now, learn the **names** well: they're what you need to spell your name and email.

id.text: Dua hal lagi yang sering membuat bingung. **W** dinamai 'double-you' (*dabel-yu*) karena dulu ditulis sebagai dua huruf U yang berdampingan. Lalu satu huruf bisa punya bunyi berbeda di kata yang berbeda; bunyi yang paling sulit akan kamu latih di pelajaran berikutnya. Untuk sekarang, kuasai dulu **nama** hurufnya: itulah yang kamu perlukan untuk mengeja nama dan email.

blocks.prompt: You spell the word 'cat' out loud. How do you say the first letter?
options: 'k', the sound at the start of cat
'see', the name of the letter C
blocks.explain: When you spell, you say each letter's name. C is called 'see', even though cat starts with a 'k' sound.

id.explain: Saat mengeja, kamu menyebut nama tiap huruf. Nama huruf C adalah 'see' (si), walaupun *cat* diawali bunyi 'k'.
id.prompt: Kamu mengeja kata 'cat' dengan suara. Bagaimana kamu menyebut huruf pertamanya?

blocks.text:
The vowel letters are **A, E, I, O, U**. All the other letters are consonants.

But wait: **Y** is in the consonant group, so why does it sometimes sound like a vowel? As a **letter**, Y counts as a consonant, and at the start of a word it sounds like Indonesian *y* (*yes, yellow*). But in *my* it sounds 'ai' and in *happy* it sounds 'i': there Y **borrows** a vowel sound. The letter group doesn't change, only the sound.

id.text:
Huruf vokal (huruf hidup) adalah **A, E, I, O, U**. Huruf lainnya konsonan (huruf mati).

Tapi tunggu: **Y** masuk kelompok konsonan, jadi kenapa kadang bunyinya seperti vokal? Sebagai **huruf**, Y dihitung konsonan, dan di awal kata bunyinya seperti *y* dalam bahasa Indonesia (*yes, yellow*). Tapi di *my* bunyinya 'ai' dan di *happy* bunyinya 'i': di situ Y **meminjam** bunyi vokal. Kelompok hurufnya tidak berubah, hanya bunyinya.

blocks.prompt: How many vowel letters are in the word 'phone'?
blocks.explain: p-h-O-n-E: the vowels are O and E. The E at the end isn't said in 'phone', but it's still a vowel letter.

id.explain: p-h-O-n-E: vokalnya O dan E. Huruf E di akhir tidak dibunyikan saat mengucapkan 'phone', tapi tetap huruf vokal.
id.prompt: Ada berapa huruf vokal di kata 'phone'?

blocks.text: To spell a word, say each **letter name** in order with a short pause. For two of the same letter together, you can say **double**: *book* is 'B, double O, K'.

id.text: Untuk mengeja, sebutkan **nama tiap huruf** berurutan dengan jeda singkat. Untuk dua huruf sama yang berdampingan, boleh pakai **double**: *book* dieja 'B, double O, K'.

blocks.prompt: Someone says: 'B, double E'. Which word is it?

id.prompt: Seseorang bilang: 'B, double E'. Kata apa itu?

blocks.text: Spelling aloud is a daily skill: giving your name at a hotel, your **email address** at work, or a code on the phone. On calls people often add a word for each letter so it isn't misheard: 'S as in Sugar'. Pilots and call centres use a fixed list called the **NATO alphabet** (Alfa, Bravo, Charlie…).

id.text: Mengeja dengan suara dipakai setiap hari: menyebut nama di hotel, **alamat email** di kantor, atau kode lewat telepon. Saat menelepon orang sering menambah satu kata per huruf supaya tidak salah dengar: 'S as in Sugar'. Pilot dan call center memakai daftar tetap bernama **alfabet NATO** (Alfa, Bravo, Charlie…).

rows.en: My email is rina at mail dot com: R-I-N-A.
rows.id: Email saya rina@mail.com: R-I-N-A. (@ dibaca 'at', titik dibaca 'dot')

rows.en: That's B as in Bravo, not D as in Delta.
rows.id: Itu B seperti Bravo, bukan D seperti Delta.

blocks.text: Practise with your own name and email address until you can say them without stopping.

id.text: Latih dengan nama dan alamat email-mu sendiri sampai bisa mengucapkannya tanpa tersendat.
